phenotype_specificity.statement: Both batch-linked girls have features the papers describe as Blau syndrome (granulomatous skin disease or rash, arthritis, uveitis). In PMID 36915122, RF, HLA-B27 and autoantibodies were negative and whole genome sequencing was done; in PMID 37386644 no PFV-related gene variant was found. Neither paper reports a full other-gene result.

quotes.quote: Her rheumatoid factor and human leukocyte antigen B27 (HLA-B27) were negative.
Her autoantibodies were negative.
Thus, we performed whole genome sequencing (WGS) for the patient and her family.
There are fourteen key genes [12] (TP53, VEGFA, Smad2, and so on) associated with it, but our patient’s case did not exhibit any genes related to PFV.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense. The batch's projection gives p.(Leu513Pro) on NP_001357395.1, whereas all three papers state p.M513T (see concerns). PMID 36915122 describes Blau-related NOD2 changes as gain-of-function in the NACHT domain.

quotes.quote: Between the two different diseases, CD-related variants are loss-of-function mutations and mainly exist in LRR, while Blau syndrome-related mutations are gain of function mutations and occur in the NACHT domain [23].

authors_classification.statement: The two batch-linked case reports give no classification; PMID 36915122 says the change has been reported previously. PMID 41673771 classifies its P9's c.1538T>C p.M513T as Likely Pathogenic (PS2+PM2+PP3+PM1+PS3+PP5).

concerns: Likely wrong locus. The papers state c.1538T>C with p.M513T; on NM_022162 (the reference named in PMID 41673771) codon 513 spans c.1537-1539, so c.1538T>C fits M513T. The batch places c.1538T>C directly on NM_001370466.1 and predicts p.(Leu513Pro), a different residue. For the other NOD2 candidates in this batch the NM_001370466.1 numbers are 81 nt lower than the papers' NM_022162 numbers, which would put the papers' variant at NM_001370466.1 c.1457T>C (Met486Thr). Neither batch-linked paper names its transcript. The panel should confirm the locus before treating this as a gap variant.
P9 in PMID 41673771 carries the same stated c.1538T>C p.M513T (on NM_022162) but is not linked to this candidate in the batch, which is consistent with the transcript problem above.
PMID 37386644 contradicts itself: it writes 'amino acid 513 from lysine to threonine' but labels the change p.M513T (Met).

Possible overlap: the 20-year-old girl in PMID 36915122 (Chinese, de novo M513T, referred to an adult hospital in 2020, later on tofacitinib) and P9 in PMID 41673771 (adult Chinese cohort at Peking Union Medical College Hospital, 2015-2025, de novo M513T) could be the same person; PMID 36915122 does not name its hospital in the text read, P9 is listed under adalimumab while the girl declined adalimumab around 2019-2020 and reported tofacitinib in December 2022, so identity is unresolved.
PMID 36915122 also lists, in its supplementary Table S, a different patient (No. 6, male) with M513A at the same codon; that is not this variant.
PMID 36915122 states the change 'has been reported previously' without a citation.
notes_for_panel: Two independent-looking de novo case reports (different ages and presentations) of a change written as c.1538T>C p.M513T, plus a third de novo carrier in PMID 41673771. The main issue is the locus: the batch's coordinates and predicted protein (Leu513Pro) do not match the papers' protein (Met513Thr).
